Suspected Kazakhstan Data Leak May Affect 16.6 Million Citizens

November 18, 2026

Posted by

Dmitry Pokidaev

Image: @depositphotos

Kazakhstan is investigating a possible leak of personal data from the Supreme Court’s information system. Cybersecurity company SOCRadar discovered a listing on the dark web offering a database allegedly containing information on 16.6 million citizens of Kazakhstan. That figure is equivalent to approximately 80% of the country’s population of 20.6 million.
Neither the authenticity of the database offered for sale nor a breach of the judicial system has been confirmed. Kazakhstan’s Judicial Administration said it was investigating the claims with the relevant government agencies. It said the unified judicial portal had undergone the required information security compliance checks. The Ministry of Artificial Intelligence and Digital Development is also examining the allegations.
The seller is asking $50,000 for what it claims are 507 million records covering the period from 2014 to 2026, organized into 186 database tables.
The database allegedly contains 13.3 million records relating to participants in court proceedings and 6.8 million records on companies. Advertised information includes individual identification numbers, passport details, court documents, administrator login details, and payment information. The listing also mentions password hashes, coded values used to verify passwords, and session tokens, which keep users logged in.
SOCRadar said that, if the claims are verified, the information could be used for financial fraud, identity theft, account takeovers, and unauthorized access to confidential court documents.
Kazakhstan has experienced several major personal data leaks in recent years. In March 2024, the State Technical Service identified a leak involving information on more than two million customers of the microfinance provider Zaimer.kz.
In June 2025, approximately 16 million records containing the names, identification numbers, addresses, and telephone numbers of citizens of Kazakhstan were discovered in publicly accessible sources. Officials later said that most of the data had been stolen in 2022 and suggested that it may have been obtained using legitimate login credentials. The National Security Committee said in April 2026 that the criminal investigation was still underway.
In August 2026, a database allegedly containing the personal information of 15 million residents of Kazakhstan was offered for sale on the dark web for about $32,000. The seller claimed to have obtained the information by hacking Kazakhstan’s e-government portal, eGov. A preliminary technical review by the ministry found no evidence that eGov’s systems had been compromised.

text:
Incident

published yesterday

National Security Agency Reports Internal Classified Network Outage During Maintenance

The National Security Agency (NSA), the primary signals intelligence organization for the United States, confirmed a network disruption on November 17, 2026. The agency described the incident as a temporary degradation of internal systems occurring during scheduled routine maintenance. The NSA maintains that mission-critical capabilities remained operational. Reports indicate the outage affected NSANet, the classified network used to transmit top-secret material.The disruption reportedly began after a software update intended to patch the system failed. Staff at the Fort Meade headquarters were notified of a code yellow alert level and non-emergency personnel were instructed to delay their arrival until noon. Internal sources suggest the network had shown signs of instability for several weeks prior to the total outage on Tuesday.The affected services include:NSANet classified communicationsInternal agency information systemsEmployee access to Fort Meade headquartersTop-secret data transmission capabilitiesAgency officials stated that the infrastructure uses multiple layers of redundancy to prevent a total loss of function during unexpected events. There is currently no evidence that the outage resulted from a cyberattack or malicious activity by a foreign actor.The NSA has not confirmed if services are fully restored but stated that its ability to defend national security continues.

text:
Incident

published yesterday

EZaccessMD Reports Data Breach Affecting Telehealth Patient Records and Medical Information

EZaccessMD, LLC, a telehealth and mobile diagnostic services provider, confirmed a data breach on September 25, 2026, after discovering suspicious activity within its computer environment. The company provides on-demand medical consultations and diagnostic imaging. Attackers exploited the company's environment between June 30 and July 30, 2026. During this window, the hackers accessed specific files and folders containing sensitive patient information. The company is currently conducting a manual review of the compromised files to identify every individual impacted by the event. The potentially exposed data includes:Social Security numbersDriver's license numbersStandardized medical diagnosis codes (ICD-10) and diagnosesLab results and prescribed medicationsPatient symptoms and physician namesDates of birth and genderFull names and physical addressesPhone numbers and relationship to primary membersThe nature of the attack and the number of affected individuals is not disclosed. EZaccessMD created a dedicated support line and is reviewing its internal security policies to prevent future incidents. The company notified the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services and is also preparing to send individual notice letters to those identified in the compromised files. Affected individuals should monitor their credit reports and financial statements for any unfamiliar activity over the next 24 months. The company recommends that patients consider placing a fraud alert or a security freeze on their credit files through major bureaus like Equifax, Experian, or TransUnion. Victims may also contact the Federal Trade Commission to report suspected identity theft.

The incident potentially exposed the names, addresses, and account numbers of hundreds of thousands of payees.**** #cybersecurity #infosec #incident #databreach https://beyondmachines.net/event_details/irish-credit-unions-report-data-breach-following-service-provider-security-incident-c-o-2-r-y/gD2P6Ple2L
text:
Incident

published Nov. 17, 2026

Irish Credit Unions Report Data Breach Following Service Provider Security Incident

The Data Protection Commission (DPC) and the Central Bank of Ireland confirmed on November 17, 2026, that dozens of credit unions have reported a suspected data breach. The Irish League of Credit Unions (ILCU) announced that the incident involves a security vulnerability at a third-party service provider. Reports indicate the affected provider is Wellington IT, a firm based in Northern Ireland that processes member account data for financial institutions.Attackers exploited a vulnerability in the service provider's systems to access information about account payees. The ILCU says that the specific vulnerability is now closed and confirmed that member account balances are secure. The ILCU represents 148 members but the incident also impacts credit unions outside of that organization.The potentially exposed data includes:Payee namesPayee account numbersPayee addressThe number of affected individuals is not disclosed, but the breach may have compromised the details of hundreds of thousands of people who paid or sent money to credit union account holders. Approximately 40 credit unions have filed formal breach notifications with the DPC so far.The DPC is assessing the notifications as a priority and the service provider continues an internal investigation. The Central Bank of Ireland has instructed all affected credit unions to communicate clearly and quickly with their members. Financial regulators and the Department of Finance are engaging with relevant parties to determine the full extent of the exposure.The Central Bank advises credit union members to contact their branch directly with any concerns about their account security. Members should be careful of any unusual communication or phishing attempts that use payee information to appear legitimate.

Attackers used injected skimmer code to steal payment card numbers, CVV codes, and expiration dates from the company's checkout page.**** #cybersecurity #infosec #incident #databreach https://beyondmachines.net/event_details/fandango-reports-payment-card-data-exposure-following-checkout-page-compromise-x-i-m-e-i/gD2P6Ple2L
text:
Incident

published Nov. 17, 2026

Fandango Reports Payment Card Data Exposure Following Checkout Page Compromise

Fandango, a major American movie ticketing platform, confirmed a data breach on November 17, 2026, after discovering unauthorized access to its checkout system. The company, which manages ticket sales for over 31,000 cinema screens and operates the Rotten Tomatoes review site, identified the issue following reports of problems on its payment page. Attackers used card skimmer code injected into the Fandango checkout page to intercept sensitive financial details as customers completed purchases. The breach occurred between October 8 and October 11, 2026. The company has since removed the malicious code and strengthened its security processes.The potentially exposed data includes:Full payment card numbersCVV security codesCard expiration datesBilling ZIP codesCustomer email addressesThe number of affected individuals is not disclosed. Regulatory filings indicate at least 913 residents in Oregon and 18 in Vermont were impacted, but a notice to the California Attorney General suggests more than 500 residents were affected in that state. Fandango claims that names, Social Security numbers, and government identification were not involved in the breach.Fandango is providing affected customers with two years of free identity protection services. These services include credit monitoring, dark web scanning, and identity theft insurance. The company has notified law enforcement.Affected individuals should monitor their financial statements for unauthorized activity and report suspicious charges to their card issuers. The company also suggests placing a fraud alert or security freeze on credit files through major reporting agencies. Customers may also consider using one-time virtual cards for future online transactions to limit exposure risks.

title: ActiveCloud : une attaque ransomware paralyse des services
text:
Le fournisseur cloud biélorusse ActiveCloud a subi une attaque par rançongiciel ayant perturbé l’hébergement de sites web, les messageries professionnelles et des serveurs virtuels.
L’entreprise a reconnu une intrusion ayant entraîné le chiffrement d’une partie de son infrastructure. Plusieurs services destinés aux entreprises sont devenus indisponibles, avec des répercussions sur les sites internet, les applications et les communications professionnelles des clients. ActiveCloud a annoncé une restauration progressive et indiqué que ses principaux services fonctionnaient à nouveau le 13 novembre. Certains clients rencontraient néanmoins encore des difficultés pour remettre leurs machines virtuelles en service. L’entreprise affirme ne pas avoir découvert d’éléments démontrant un vol de données, sans avoir identifié publiquement les responsables ni le vecteur initial de l’intrusion.
Des services cloud touchés simultanément
Les attaquants sont parvenus à chiffrer certains éléments de l’infrastructure ActiveCloud.
L’incident a notamment affecté les offres E-Cloud, E-Cloud Protected et SmartMail, utilisées pour l’hébergement, les serveurs virtuels et la messagerie professionnelle.
La compromission a provoqué des interruptions chez plusieurs clients. Le média biélorusse Smartpress a confirmé utiliser l’infrastructure concernée.
Des perturbations ont également été rapportées sur les services numériques de Domino’s Pizza en Biélorussie.
La restauration des principales plateformes ne signifiait pas la résolution immédiate de tous les problèmes individuels.
Des hébergeurs confrontés à des attaques destructrices
L’incident est survenu dans un contexte de cyberattaques contre plusieurs prestataires d’hébergement de la région. Le fournisseur ESTT avait signalé le 8 novembre une attaque par rançongiciel visant son infrastructure cloud. Un autre opérateur, Beget, avait précédemment été confronté à une intrusion au cours de laquelle des scripts destructeurs avaient effacé certaines données.
Chez Beget, la perte de sauvegardes de serveurs virtuels a compliqué les opérations de reconstruction.

Damien Bancal est une figure incontournable de la cybersécurité, reconnu à l’international pour son expertise et son engagement depuis plus de 30 ans. Fondateur de ZATAZ.com en 1989 (et DataSecurityBreach.fr en 2015), il a fait de ce média une référence majeure en matière de veille, d’alertes et d’analyses sur les cybermenaces. Auteur de 17 ouvrages et de plusieurs centaines d’articles pour des médias comme Le Monde, France Info ou 01net, il vulgarise les enjeux du piratage informatique et de la protection des données personnelles.

Lauréat du prix spécial du livre au FIC/InCyber 2022, finaliste du premier CTF Social Engineering nord-américain (2023), et vainqueur du CTF Social Engineering du HackFest Canada (2024), il est reconnu pour sa capacité à allier pratique du terrain et transmission pédagogique. Le New York Times ou encore Le Big Data ont salué son parcours, et l’agence Tyto PR l’a classé parmi les 500 personnalités tech les plus influentes en 2023. Il est aujourd’hui 9ᵉ influenceur cyber en Europe.

Chroniqueur à la radio et à la télévision (France Info, RTL, M6, Medi1...), il est également réserviste citoyen au sein de la Gendarmerie Nationale (Lieutenant-Colonel - Unité Nationale Cyber) et de l'Éducation Nationale (Hauts-de-France). Médaillé de la Défense Nationale (Marine) et des réservistes volontaires, il poursuit son engagement au travers de son entreprise veillezataz.com, lancée en 2022.

title: TSMC : des données de salariés dérobées chez un prestataire
text:
Le fabricant taïwanais de semi-conducteurs TSMC confirme une fuite de données concernant des salariés actuels et anciens, consécutive à la compromission d’un fournisseur cloud.
L’entreprise a informé les autorités financières américaines de l’incident dans un document réglementaire. Ses investigations indiquent que les données concernées correspondaient aux informations stockées dans les services d’un prestataire cloud, dont le nom n’a pas été communiqué. TSMC affirme que ses propres systèmes n’ont pas été compromis et que les informations ne concernent ni ses opérations industrielles ni ses clients. Cette confirmation intervient après l’apparition, sur un forum cybercriminel, d’une proposition de vente portant sur 6,9 Go de données présentées comme appartenant à ses employés.
Une annonce criminelle précédant la confirmation officielle
Le 8 novembre 2026, un individu a proposé sur un forum de cybercriminalité un ensemble de données prétendument issues de TSMC.
L’annonce mentionnait 6,9 Go d’informations comprenant, selon son auteur, des coordonnées, des éléments d’identification et des informations bancaires.
Le vendeur exigeait trois bitcoins, présentés dans l’article original comme représentant environ 200 000 dollars au moment des faits.
Cette proposition commerciale constitue une revendication criminelle. Les catégories précises et le volume des données effectivement dérobées n’ont pas tous été confirmés publiquement par TSMC.
La société a néanmoins reconnu une compromission impliquant son prestataire cloud.
Une nouvelle illustration du risque fournisseur
TSMC indique travailler avec le prestataire concerné, les autorités compétentes et une entreprise spécialisée en cybersécurité.
Des démarches d’information et d’accompagnement des personnes touchées ont également été engagées.
L’entreprise souligne que ses systèmes internes et ses activités industrielles n’ont pas été compromis dans cet incident.
Ce point est important : la compromission d’informations personnelles chez un fournisseur ne signifie pas nécessairement une intrusion dans les infrastructures de production ou de recherche du donneur d’ordre.
L’affaire rappelle aussi que les données de salariés peuvent constituer une cible indépendante des secrets industriels.
Pour le renseignement cyber, la surveillance des annonces criminelles doit être accompagnée d’une vérification de l’origine des données et du périmètre réel de la compromission.

title: Java4Shell, une faille critique dans OpenJDK
text:
Une vulnérabilité d’OpenJDK expose plusieurs applications d’entreprise à l’exécution de code à distance. Oracle a publié un correctif le 17 novembre, après le signalement de chercheurs.
Référencée CVE-2026-114938, la faille Java4Shell concerne une fonction de décodage Base64 dans l’environnement d’exécution Java. Les chercheurs de Calif ont démontré des effets sur plusieurs applications, dont Jenkins, Jira, Confluence et Keycloak, dans les configurations qu’ils ont testées. Le risque dépend notamment de la version de Java, du processeur et de l’usage de la fonction vulnérable par l’application. Calif attribue à la faille un score de 9,2. Oracle retient 8,1 dans son bulletin de novembre, avec une autre version de la méthode de notation CVSS. La mise à jour doit être vérifiée auprès du fournisseur de chaque distribution Java déployée.
Une faille dans le moteur Java partagé par plusieurs logiciels
Le décodage Base64 intervient dans de nombreuses applications qui échangent des données. Ici, la vulnérabilité touche une variante accélérée de cette fonction sur certains processeurs x86-64. La corruption de mémoire qui en résulte peut, selon Calif, conduire à la divulgation de données ou à l’exécution de code à distance. Plusieurs distributions fondées sur OpenJDK sont concernées, notamment Oracle Java SE, Amazon Corretto, Eclipse Temurin et Azul Zulu.
Dans les essais de Calif, certains produits se sont révélés exposés avant authentification, tandis que d’autres exigeaient déjà un accès. Cette distinction compte pour la réponse des équipes de sécurité. Une application accessible depuis Internet et exploitable avant connexion présente une exposition différente de celle d’un service interne exigeant des identifiants. Ces résultats décrivent des démonstrations de recherche. Les sources consultées ne documentent aucune attaque en cours liée à cette faille.
Le correctif se joue au niveau de l’environnement d’exécution
Oracle a publié son bulletin de sécurité le 17 novembre. Pour les équipes chargées du déploiement, l’inventaire doit couvrir les environnements Java utilisés par les applications, y compris ceux livrés avec un produit. Calif recommande, lorsqu’une mise à jour immédiate est impossible, de désactiver temporairement l’optimisation concernée. L’installation d’une version corrigée traite la vulnérabilité elle-même.
En veille cyber, la présence d’une même brique Java dans plusieurs produits impose de rapprocher les bulletins des éditeurs de l’inventaire des instances réellement déployées.

The Booba Project ransomware group has allegedly listed the Clinton Assessors Board, a US local government entity operating at www.clintonma.gov, on its dark web leak site. According to the threat actor, the attack was purportedly carried out on November 17, 2026, and the group claims to have exfiltrated approximately 7 GB of data described as “Government Administration” material.
This claim has NOT been independently verified by Yazoul Security or any third party. The listing appears on a ransomware group’s leak site, which is a self-published assertion by the threat actor and should be treated with skepticism until corroborated. No sample files, proof-of-exfiltration artifacts, or victim confirmation have been publicly validated at the time of writing.
Threat Actor Profile
Booba Project is a relatively low-profile ransomware operation. Based on currently available intelligence, the group’s total known victim count is unknown, and there is no public research available documenting its tooling, infrastructure, or operational history. Its known tools and tactics are not publicly documented at this time.
Because Booba Project lacks a well-established, independently tracked track record, its credibility cannot be confidently assessed. Ransomware groups with limited public visibility sometimes exaggerate data volumes, inflate victim counts, or recycle previously breached data to manufacture leverage. The absence of known tooling or prior research means defenders should not assume a specific TTP set when assessing exposure. Yazoul Security does not currently have YARA rules or detection signatures attributed to this group; monitoring for generic ransomware precursor behaviors (credential access, lateral movement, bulk archive creation) remains advisable.
Alleged Data Exposure
The group claims to have stolen 7 GB of data categorized as “Government Administration.” If accurate, such material could plausibly include internal correspondence, administrative records, or operational documents. However, the specific contents, sensitivity, and whether the data genuinely originates from the Clinton Assessors Board have not been confirmed. No data samples, file listings, or download references are included in this report by policy. The 7 GB figure is a self-reported claim and may be overstated.
Potential Impact
If the claim is substantiated, potential impacts could include exposure of administrative records, reputational harm to the municipality, and possible regulatory or notification obligations under applicable state and local government data-handling rules. Local government entities often hold constituent information, which raises privacy considerations if personal data is among the allegedly stolen files. At this stage, all impact scenarios are speculative and contingent on verification.
What to Watch For

Official statements from the Clinton Assessors Board or the Town of Clinton confirming or denying any incident.
Independent confirmation of data exfiltration, such as breach notifications or regulatory filings.
Appearance of the alleged data on other channels, which could corroborate or contradict the group’s claim.

Un nouvel antisémitisme ? Avec Michel Wieviorka

1 min. de lecture

Citer

Partager

Imprimeren PDF

Ajouter aux favoris

Pascal Boniface

Directeur de l’IRIS

Michel Wieviorka
Sociologue et directeur d’études émérite à l’EHESS

Ce 15 novembre, l’American Jewish Committee (AJC) a publié l’édition 2027 de La radiographie de l’antisémitisme en France, relayée par Le Parisien, déclarant que la société française était sujette à une vague massive et durable d’antisémitisme depuis les attentats du Hamas le 7 octobre en 2023. Certains commentateurs parlent de « nouvel antisémitisme » pour qualifier un phénomène qui serait d’après eux avant tout porté par la gauche radicale et les musulmans français, sur fond d’hostilité à Israël.

Pourtant, la montée de l’antisémitisme est loin d’être nouvelle. Elle ressurgit dès la fin des années 1970 avec la négation de la Shoah par l’extrême-droite. Aujourd’hui, la haine des juifs demeure très implantée au sein de ce camp politique, bien que l’attention médiatique et politique pointe généralement du doigt la gauche. La confusion régulièrement alimentée entre critique d’Israël et antisémitisme brouille par ailleurs la compréhension des mutations que connait l’antisémitisme contemporain.

Comment interpréter les chiffres décrivant une montée de l’antisémitisme ? Existe-t-il un « nouvel antisémitisme » aux ressorts et causes différents de celui qui existait au XIXe et XXe siècles ? Comment expliquer le silence des médias et du gouvernement sur l’antisémitisme d’extrême-droite ? Ces enjeux soulèvent plus largement la question de la place laissée au débat intellectuel en France : les sciences sociales ont-elles encore un impact sur les décisions politiques ?

Autant d’enjeux abordés avec Michel Wieviorka, sociologue et directeur d’études émérite à l’EHESS.

title: Corvette européenne : quelle opportunité pour la Marine nationale ?
text:
Corvette européenne : quelle opportunité pour la Marine nationale ?

Publié le
18/11/2026

Analyse

À Euronaval 2026, Naval Group, Fincantieri et Navantia ont signé un accord pour poursuivre le développement de l’European Patrol Corvette (EPC). Alors que la France doit remplacer ses frégates de surveillance Floréal, sa participation à ce programme européen reste incertaine, malgré ses perspectives opérationnelles et industrielles.

Le remplacement des six frégates légères Floréal, en service depuis les années 1990, a été repoussé à l’horizon 2034. La Marine nationale doit désormais définir leurs successeurs, capables d’assurer des missions de présence et de surveillance outre-mer tout en faisant face à des menaces aériennes, de surface et sous-marines. L’autonomie à la mer constitue une exigence majeure pour surveiller les quelque 10,2 millions de km² d’espaces maritimes français, répartis sur l’ensemble des océans. Si une corvette nationale éprouvée, comme la Gowind, reste une option, l’EPC pourrait offrir un compromis différent mais pertinent.

I. Le renouvellement des Floréal, une occasion de renforcer le second rang

Le remplacement des Floréal doit permettre de dépasser leur vocation initiale de surveillance et de protection des espaces maritimes outre-mer. Ces bâtiments assurent aujourd’hui des missions variées, allant du contrôle des zones économiques exclusives à la lutte contre les trafics et la piraterie, notamment dans l’océan Indien. Malgré leur appellation de « frégates », ces bâtiments d’environ 3 000 tonnes disposent de capacités de combat plus que limitées. Conçus pour évoluer dans des environnements peu contestés, ils répondent de moins en moins aux menaces susceptibles de peser sur les espaces maritimes français.

Depuis la conception des Floréal, le rôle comme les capacités des corvettes ont profondément évolué. Les progrès de l’électronique, des systèmes de combat et de l’intégration des armements permettent désormais à des bâtiments d’environ 3 000 tonnes de disposer de missiles antiaériens, de moyens de lutte anti-sous-marine et de capteurs autrefois réservés à des frégates plus importantes. Cette montée en capacité répond aussi à l’évolution des missions. Les tensions dans le détroit d’Ormuz rappellent que la surveillance et l’escorte peuvent désormais exposer les bâtiments à des drones et à des missiles. Un véritable échelon corvette permettrait ainsi de renforcer la présence armée et d’assurer certaines escortes sans mobiliser systématiquement les frégates françaises.

Le renforcement des capacités de combat devra toutefois préserver les capacités de patrouille renforcée attribuées aux Floréal. Une exigence récemment rappelée par l’amiral Christophe Cluzel devant les parlementaires : «Nous avons besoin de bâtiments capables de faire face à l’ensemble des menaces contemporaines : menaces aériennes, sous-marines ou de surface. Telle est précisément la vocation de ces futurs bâtiments. Je serai également extrêmement vigilant quant à leur endurance, compte tenu des distances considérables auxquelles nous sommes habitués, notamment outre-mer»

II. L’EPC, le choix du volume utile

Le programme EPC présente l’intérêt de couvrir l’ensemble des missions attendues du futur second rang français. Il prévoit deux versions principales autour d’une architecture commune d’environ 3 000 tonnes : la Full Combat Multipurpose (FCM), davantage orientée vers le combat naval, et la Long Range Multipurpose (LRM), privilégiant les missions prolongées. Ce périmètre offre à la Marine nationale plusieurs possibilités, entre une version française équilibrée ou une flotte associant les deux variantes. L’objectif serait de disposer de bâtiments capables d’assurer les missions les plus exigeantes de surveillance et de police maritime, tout en constituant un premier échelon de combat lorsque la situation l’impose.

L’autre intérêt de l’EPC tient à sa modularité, une caractéristique encore peu répandue sur les bâtiments de combat […]

Ajouter aux favoris

Christophe Ventura

Directeur de recherche à l’IRIS, responsable du Programme Amérique latine/Caraïbe

Dans la nuit du 2 au 3 novembre 2026, la Banque centrale du Paraguay (BCP) a placé sous tutelle la banque numérique Ueno Bank pour insolvabilité, gelant les dépôts financiers de près de trois millions de clients, soit près de la moitié de la population. Très populaire grâce à des offres promotionnelles alléchantes, la banque avait réussi à capter 850 millions de dollars de fonds publics grâce à ses liens étroits avec le pouvoir exécutif. Cette affaire entraîna dans sa chute le président Santiago Peña, qui détenait des actions dans la société mère. Face aux importantes mobilisations de la population à Asunción, Santiago Peña présente sa démission le 5 novembre. Le Parlement l’a toutefois rejetée, préférant engager directement une procédure de destitution à son encontre. Ce scandale politico-financier interroge alors sur comment naissent et se reproduisent des sociétés oligarchiques qui mettent en péril, sont capables de mettre en péril l’ensemble d’une société sur le plan économique pour servir leurs propres intérêts.

Quelle est l’origine de ce scandale ? Au-delà des frontières du Paraguay, quelles sont les ramifications internationales de l’affaire Ueno Bank ? Enfin, que révèle cette crise sur les relations entre le pouvoir politique et les milieux financiers ?

Nouvelle chronique de l’Amérique latine avec Christophe Ventura, directeur de recherche à l’IRIS et responsable du Programme Amérique latine/Caraïbe.

title: DETOURNER WERO AU PROFIT DE L’OSINT
text:
DETOURNER WERO AU PROFIT DE L’OSINT

Le Contractuel

Publié le
18/11/2026

Analyse

L’OSINT, acronyme anglais d’Open Source Intelligence ou renseignement ne sources ouvertes, repose sur une méthodologie d’enquête et la connaissance d’outils actionnables. Certaines qualités comme la curiosité et l’inventivité sont des atouts supplémentaires en faveur des analystes. Cet article n’a pas seulement vocation à diffuser de nouveaux pivots, c’est-à-dire passer d’une information à une autre, mais aussi à démontrer aux analystes OSINT débutants qu’il est possible de détourner des outils et applications de tous les jours au profit de leurs investigations.

D’abord, présentons Wero. Il s’agit d’un système de paiement instantané européen utilisé pour les virements de compte à compte en temps réel. Il s’appuie sur l’application mobile Wero. Le service lie directement un numéro de téléphone mobile à un compte bancaire pour simplifier l’identification et les transferts. Il est actuellement opérationnel en France, en Belgique et en Allemagne et son déploiement aux autres États européens est prévu de manière progressive.

D’un numéro de téléphone à une identité partielle

Wero simplifie les virements entre des comptes bancaires en autorisant les transferts d’argent (demande et réception) par numéro de téléphone. Lorsqu’un utilisateur entre un numéro de téléphone, l’identité partielle et parfois totale du bénéficiaire est affichée si ce même numéro est associé à Wero. Le nom complet est affiché uniquement si l’utilisateur a activé l’option « afficher le nom complet » ou s’il s’agit d’un compte bancaire d’entreprise.

Exemple d’un numéro associé à un compte bancaire sur l’application mobile Wero.

Cette application est donc utile pour vérifier l’identité du détenteur d’un numéro de téléphone. Il peut s’agir d’une vérification, si vous devez confirmer qu’un individu détient toujours cette coordonnée, ou d’une première piste afin de poursuivre vos investigations avec un prénom et un nom partiel. D’ailleurs, gardez à l’esprit que les astérisques correspondent bien au nombre de lettres du patronyme du bénéficiaire. Pour Margot P****** (exemple ci-dessus), son nom de famille est donc composé de 7 lettres.

Pivoter d’une adresse mail à un numéro de téléphone

Le bon vieux temps, n’est-ce pas ? Et bien c’est de nouveau possible, sous certaines conditions, grâce à Wero.

Prenons l’exemple de l’adresse mail Exxx@Exxx.net, détenue par E. E.

La première étape est de se connecter sur un outil tiers, payant et spécialisé dans l’identification d’informations liées à des coordonnées, comme Lol Archiver ou Osint Industries. Il suffit de se rendre dans la section « Email Reverse » pour le premier et l’interface de recherche pour le second. Renseignez l’adresse mail et laisser les modules rechercher les comptes d’applications ou sites bancaires liés à cette coordonnée. Si l’adresse mail est utilisée sur AirBnb ou sur Deliveroo, vous obtenez l’indicatif ainsi que les 2 derniers chiffres du numéro.

Exemple des résultats de la recherche par mail sur Lol Archiver et Osint Industries.

Il existait précédemment un module Lol Archiver permettant d’effectuer automatiquement une recherche mot de passe oublié sur le site client de Samsung. Il faut désormais vérifier manuellement si l’utilisateur détient un compte associé à l’adresse mail Exxx@Exxx.net. En l’occurrence, oui, vous vous en doutez. Samsung dévoile des informations supplémentaires : les 2 premiers chiffres du numéro, et 2 chiffres centraux.

Processus de récupération de mot de passe de compte client sur Samsung.

A ce stade, il manque seulement 2 chiffres au numéro de téléphone détenu par E.E., le +33.06.**.51.6X.3X (* = inconnu, X = censuré). C’est là que Wero intervient. Il suffit de taper une par une les combinaisons possibles dans l’application mobile en espérant que le numéro de téléphone soit bien associé à Wero. Dans notre cas, évidemment, E. E. est un utilisateur de cette application […]

title: Ukraine Straddles Diverging Fronts
text: Striking in the deep: Firefighters at the scene of a Russian drone strike on the 15th-century Bernardine Church and Monastery, a UNESCO World Heritage Site in central Lviv. Image: Olena Z / Zuma Press Inc / Alamy StockUkraine’s battlefield prospects are improving while Russian forces deteriorate, but damage is accumulating in the rear and funding for its resistance is far from assured.The unsurprising failure of US diplomatic efforts to negotiate a termination to Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine will see the conflict protract into its sixth year. The dynamics of the conflict in 2027 will be characterised by the diverging trends between the front, where Ukraine is gaining the advantage, and the rear, where Russia retains hopes of success. Shifting Putin’s intransigence requires that Ukraine and its partners deny him a viable path to military victory and set out a clear plan to resource Ukrainian success beyond the winter.The Fortress HoldsIn Donbas, Russian forces are conducting a high intensity of attacks at the northern and southern ends of Ukraine’s fortress belt to set conditions to seize Slovyansk and Kramatorsk in 2027. Despite a massive commitment of manpower and fires, they are failing, with unprecedented casualty rates of more than 35,000 a month. While the Russians may make some progress as the weather decreases the efficiency of Ukrainian UAV operations in late November, Russia is now losing more personnel than it is recruiting, such that its forces are on track to shrink in size for the first year since 2022.Russian forces are not only declining quantitatively but are qualitatively degrading under the pressure of attrition. As a result, Ukraine has been able to conduct small but successful counterattacks along the front, demonstrating a growing capacity for combined arms manoeuvre in some formations. As winter sets in and the density of cover declines, attacks on Russian logistics and advancing troops are destined to see casualties remain high. This should leave Russian forces vulnerable in the spring.As Russian forces now threaten to contest the hills at the centre of Ukraine’s ‘fortress belt’, Kyiv can no longer trade space for time and must counterattack. Its capacity to do so at greater scale will be determined by the extent to which it can build up reserves and coordinate its forces. Progress has been made in consolidating Ukraine’s new Army Corps, but increasing the scale of Ukrainian gains will depend upon better coordination of close fighting and strikes on Russian logistics and command and control, closing the gap between Ukraine’s ground and unmanned systems forces.A Race to the MiddleFor much of 2026, Ukraine has waged an aggressive ‘middle strike’ campaign on Russian forces. British hackers face prison for GTA 6 data breach and crypto thefts

Zack Whittaker

6:55 AM PST · November 18, 2026

Two British hackers are facing lengthy prison sentences for separate hacks as part of their roles in long-running, prolific cybercriminal hacking groups. The two are accused of hacks that stole millions of dollars in cryptocurrency and leaked pre-release footage from Grand Theft Auto VI.

Tyler Buchanan, 24, from Dundee, Scotland, has been sentenced to six years by a U.S. court after he was extradited to the United States in 2025. Buchanan was accused of stealing at least $11 million in cryptocurrency from dozens of companies as part of a phishing scheme. The attacks would impersonate IT helpdesks and call up unsuspecting employees and trick them into giving over their credentials, which the hackers would use to break in and steal cryptocurrency.

Meanwhile, Arion Kurtaj, 21, from Oxford, England, has pleaded guilty to several cyberattacks that he carried out while a teenager. One hack included the theft of data and extortion of Rockstar Games, the maker of Grand Theft Auto VI, which was released Wednesday after several delays.

Kurtaj was previously ordered by a U.K. court to be detained indefinitely after deeming him unable to stand trial due to his autism diagnosis and his perceived high hacking risk to the public. But U.K. authorities, tasked with charging Kurtaj with cybercrime offenses, confirmed Monday that he had admitted to several hacks, including leaking footage of the long-awaited video game, and would subsequently face a public trial.

U.K. authorities confirmed earlier reporting that Kurtaj hacked several companies, including while he was confined to a hotel amid police protection from rival criminal gangs. The authorities said Kurtaj used an Amazon Fire TV stick to hack the companies, which breached his bail conditions.

Both Buchanan and Kurtaj were members of overlapping cybercriminal groups, dubbed 0ktapus, Lapsus$, and later Scattered Spider. These prolific hacking gangs mostly consist of teenagers and young male adults, lending to the term “advanced persistent teenagers,” whose focus and motivations were to steal as much money as possible through various cyberattacks.

Over the years, the hackers were collectively responsible for hundreds of cyberattacks targeting big companies, including Coinbase, DoorDash, Mailchimp, and Nvidia.

By late 2024, both U.K. and U.S. authorities say they had indicted five of the hackers whom they believed were key members of the hacking groups, including Buchanan. The U.S. Department of Justice said this week that Buchanan is the fifth and final defendant to be sentenced in this case.

The suspected Chinese advanced persistent threat (APT) group behind the sophisticated EggStreme malware has rebuilt its toolkit as it continues to target government organizations in the Philippines.

"When attackers are exposed, the cheap response is to rotate," Bitdefender said in a technical report shared with The Hacker News. "A file hash changes with every recompile, a domain costs a few dollars, and a new IP address costs less."

"The EggStreme operators did more than rotate – the agent we now see uses a different network protocol, has an enhanced command set, and comes in a passive variant that never beacons out. The infrastructure appears to be moving away from the one certificate authority that tied its older servers together."

The end result is that the changes allow it to bypass static signatures and heuristic detections built around the EggStreme malware framework when it was first exposed in September 2025.

Delivered via an as-yet-unknown initial access vector, EggStreme's defining characteristic is the use of DLL sideloading to execute payloads. It features multiple components as follows -

EggStremeFuel (aka RawCookie), which conducts system profiling and deploys EggStremeLoader
EggStremeLoader, which sets up persistence and decrypts and executes EggStremeReflectiveLoader
EggStremeReflectiveLoader, which executes EggStremeAgent
EggStremeAgent (aka Gorem RAT), the core component and a full-featured backdoor that enables system reconnaissance, lateral movement, data theft via an injected keylogger called EggStremeKeylogger, and reverse shell and file upload/download capabilities via a secondary backdoor called EggStremeWizard

It's worth noting that some components of the framework, such as EggStremeFuel and EggStremeLoader, have been put to use by another cluster tracked by Palo Alto Networks as CL-STA-1048 between March and September 2025.

Martin Zugec, technical solutions director at Bitdefender, told The Hacker News that CL-STA-1048's targeting of a Southeast Asian government entity and its associated tooling is "consistent with what we have observed" but emphasized that their research is more focused on the malware's capabilities and its evolution rather than attribution.

As is often the case with Chinese-aligned activity, the same tools can be used by more than one threat actor, Zugec noted, adding they have not compared infrastructure or victim data to determine if the two sets of activity constitute the same threat cluster as CL-STA-1048.

The latest findings from Bitdefender show a significant retooling of EggStreme's capabilities, including removing the keylogger from every agent build observed since then. Within two weeks after public disclosure, the threat actors are also said to have made other changes -

The method EggStremeFuel uses to protect its configuration
EggStremeLoader's cryptography and payload format, moving from RC4 to RC5 and to a custom cipher by the end of October 2025
Added commands in EggStremeAgent that facilitate Active Directory reconnaissance, Windows Management Instrumentation (WMI) querying, TCP traffic forwarding, and execution of PowerShell, Portable Executable (PE), .NET assembly payloads
Moving from a single certificate authority to campaign-specific certificate authorities

In addition, where lateral movement previously relied on Impacket-like tooling and on EggStremeAgent itself, newer incidents make use of an unmanaged system that sits outside of the organization's endpoint management but is still reachable by other workstations to stage the payloads and launch them via DLL sideloading using a Visual Basic Script (VBScript) file […]

EngineeringUsing a "chaos loop" to harden the Claude Docs launch: 60 server errors across billions of requestsClaude Docs is a doc editor that you, your teammates, and Claude all work in together. The interesting part is that a Claude session anywhere, from chat to Claude Code, can open the same doc and read, write, and comment in it live, right next to you. We released Docs on September 16, 2026. This post is about the service that runs underneath it.AUTHORVivek NairCATEGORYEngineeringPUBLISHEDNov 17, 2026READING TIME9 min Three weeks before Claude Docs opened to the public, it was running as a proof of concept on a single node, used by a few thousand people inside Anthropic. We were racing toward an ambitious launch date, and our own estimate said we'd see millions of docs within the first few days.
We launched on September 16. By September 22, people had created over 4.6 million docs. Across 2 billion requests we saw only 60 server errors, and we never had to roll back. The whole Docs service ran on about 50 memory-optimized pods.
Two decisions got us there:

A chaos loop at launch scale. We set up a test harness on our staging environment where Claude ran constantly for two weeks to try and break the service. It load tested every part of our infrastructure and fixed whatever fell over.
Improving legibility to Claude. Claude could only close the loop effectively on fixes if our system produced accurate telemetry every iteration. We made a call early to avoid any runtime that uses memory or CPU in ways our code can't easily control (e.g. runtimes with garbage collection). When a telemetry signal looked concerning, Claude could easily trace it to a bug or a specific design decision.

But honestly, this only worked because our frontier models have gotten much better recently (I used an internal research model roughly comparable to Claude Fable 5.2). In our experience, they can now stick with one goal through a run like this for weeks, which is what helped us hit launch scale in a tight timeline.
THE CHAOS LOOP
A few thousand internal users on one machine told us nothing about whether the service would survive launch, and we obviously didn't have launch traffic to test with.
We wanted real evidence to decide how fast we could roll out. So on September 4, about two weeks before launch, I had Claude drive a staging cluster that mirrored production at over a million synthetic docs a day and break core components on purpose. And then... I just left it running (I've included the full cost at the end of this article).
My setup was pretty simple. The loop was a session in Claude Code that I left running: pick a scenario, run the harness, read the telemetry, propose a fix, ship it to staging, repeat. That session acted as a coordinator and handed most of the work to sub-agents. In the busiest week, that usually meant about 11 sub-agents running at a time, and 30 at the peak. The coordinator also talked to our internal variant of Claude Tag (beta) via the Slack MCP to learn from other infrastructure teams at Anthropic who had scaled similar services. Their agents checked our scaling approach for pitfalls they’d already hit.
The fun part was picking scenarios I thought were paranoid:

10M new docs created in a single day
22,000 live connections reconnecting at once
One hot doc with hundreds of viewers, a server killed while it was still loading a doc, and the database stalling

Each iteration looked the same. Our testing harness selected a feature like document creation and pushed creation to saturation. Claude then read telemetry using the Datadog MCP and came back with a short menu of options and a recommendation.
If the recommendation was easy to undo, Claude wrote and deployed the change to staging and reran the test. We had telemetry on every operation the service ran. Every database query, for example, reported its name and how many rows it scanned versus how many it returned, so Claude could spot a bad query and rewrite it.

Google on Tuesday announced the release of Chrome 158 to the stable channel with patches for 204 vulnerabilities, including six critical-severity bugs.

The critical flaws include three use-after-free issues in WebView, GarbageCollection, and WebAudio, out-of-bounds write defects in GPU and ANGLE, and a buffer overflow in Media.

No bug bounty reward will be paid for any of these. In fact, no reward will be handed out for 163 of the security weaknesses. Google and Xinyang Ge discovered 145 and 15 of them, respectively.

Of the remaining vulnerabilities, 62 are high-severity issues, 82 are medium-severity, and 54 are low-severity.

Google says it handed out $11,000 in rewards for five of the vulnerabilities reported by external researchers and has yet to determine the amounts to be paid for 36 flaws.

The most common type of vulnerability patched in Chrome 158 is use-after-free (51 occurrences), followed by incorrect authorization (34), missing authorization (16), out-of-bounds write/read (15), uninitialized resource (14), information leak (11), UI misrepresentation (10), improper input validation (9), and race condition (8).

Google makes no mention of any of these vulnerabilities being exploited in the wild, but users are advised to update their browsers as soon as possible.

The latest Chrome iteration is now rolling out as versions 158.0.8127.36/.37 for Windows and macOS, and as version 158.0.8127.36 for Linux.

As federal agencies revise their strategies for implementing post-quantum encryption by President Donald Trump’s new 2030 deadline, agency leaders and federal contractors are mulling over how to adapt the new protections to older, legacy technology and address gaps in visibility over federal encryption protocols.

Dan Pomeroy, deputy associate administrator at the Office of Technology Policy at the General Services Administration, said his agency focused first on the smart Personal Identity Verification (PIV) cards that grant employees access to GSA facilities, computers and the authority to sign official documents.

Pomeroy said agency technologists ran new post-quantum encryption algorithms directly onto the card chip, issued new credentials, and built the surrounding policies, certifications and hardware security modules to support the transition.

Post-quantum cryptography tends to require larger keys and signatures, along with a fast, reliable network connection to process larger amounts of data. That could be a problem for assets like satellites, which have weaker connections. But in many cases, agencies can switch to newer algorithms using the same systems, data and devices already in use throughout the government.

“That work demonstrated that quantum-resistant credentials are not theoretical, they are achievable with the cards we have today, the technology we have today,” said Pomeroy Tuesday at FedTalks presented by FedScoop.

Pomeroy also said the government constantly needs to test for bugs and interoperability issues. His agency works with contractors to make sure they use post-quantum algorithms “from the start” and bring the necessary infrastructure to support the agency’s encryption efforts.

An executive order issued earlier this year moved the mandatory federal deadline for completing the post-quantum transition from 2035 to 2030. Major private-sector organizations like Google have set similar internal timelines of 2029 for their own encryption switchovers, citing similar concerns.

The order cut by more than half the time agencies were originally given to transition their public key encryption. While national security officials have cited threats like “harvest now, decrypt later” in pushing for faster adoption, experts say that encryption switchovers are often measured in decades.

Vanessa Hunt, general manager for federal markets at IBM, said many federal agencies have “blind spots” in their network, particularly in areas where “the sensitivity of the data outlives the approach protecting it.”

Additionally, encryption protocols are often spread across different datasets, identities, infrastructure and networks, making it difficult to map everything that needs to be upgraded.

“I think the biggest blind spot right now is just the visibility,” said Hunt. “I think it’s easier to know where our sensitive data lives, it’s less easy to know where the cryptography that protects it is.”

Texas-based dental services provider Access Dental Management (ADM) has disclosed a data breach impacting more than 340,000 individuals.

Providing dental care across Texas and in Illinois, Indiana, and New Mexico, ADM says it discovered the incident on May 5 and immediately began an investigation with help from third-party forensic specialists.

The investigation determined that, between May 1 and May 4, hackers had accessed its network and viewed or copied certain data, including personal information.

On October 21, ADM’s review of the compromised information determined that the attacker accessed names, addresses, dates of birth, Social Security numbers, medical information, and health insurance information.

“Upon learning of this incident, ADM moved quickly to investigate and respond to the incident. As part of its ongoing commitment to the security of information, ADM is reviewing and enhancing its existing policies and procedures related to data privacy to reduce the likelihood of a similar future incident,” ADM said in a notice (PDF).

Last week, the organization notified the Texas and Vermont Attorney General’s Offices that 341,049 individuals were affected by the data breach (341,039 in Texas and 10 in Vermont), but the total number could reportedly surpass 455,000.

ADM is sending written notification letters to the potentially affected individuals, encouraging them “to remain vigilant against incidents of identity theft and fraud by reviewing your account statements, explanation of benefits forms, and monitoring your free credit reports for suspicious activity and to detect errors.”

While the organization did not share further details on the cyberattack, the WorldLeaks ransomware group claimed responsibility for the intrusion on June 5.

SecurityWeek has emailed ADM’s parent platform Surge Private Equity for additional information on the incident and will update this article if it responds.
